full_judgment: 7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that both the courts below during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed gross illegality and irregularity and without considering the material evidence on record they committed error of law in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that the lower appellate court without discussing and considering the evidence of the witnesses decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the plaintiffs on surmise and conjecture and without discussions upon the issues framed upheld the findings of the trial court which is violative of the provisions laid down in Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Both the courts below failed to consider that the plaintiffs are claiming title and partition on the basis of kabla deeds marked as exhibit-3 series and same private documents of koda pattan exhibits-2, 2(ka). Having failed to prove these documents under sections 67 and 68 of the Evidence Act and in absence of proof of its execution the documents does not create any presumption of its genuineness and thereby committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate also submits that the courts below were totally failed to assess the material exhibits of the defendants marked as Exhibits-`Ka' and gala' series. They also failed to evaluate Exhibit-'1Ca' properly. The learned lower appellate court acted illegally in affirming the decree of the trial court ignoring the oral and documentary evidence of the defendants by resorting to hypothetical assumption and both the courts below erred in law in not considering the respective cases of the parties in jaxta position with same yardstick weightment and rejected the defendant's case as regard title without proper application of judicial mind and the same has caused miscarriage of justice. The learned Advocate lastly submits that in the impugned judgment and decree there has been apparent misreading and non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be interfered with.
